mechanics.name: Boon: Dark Theory
mechanics.currentEffect: Bless a Dull or Hex Totem. Survivors within 24 metres gain 3% Haste; the effect lingers for 2/3/4 seconds after leaving its range.
activation: Bless a Dull or Hex Totem.
Be within 24 metres for the main Haste effect.
Ends/deactivates when: Effect ends after leaving range and the tiered linger time, or when the totem is snuffed.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.7.0): Increased Haste from 2% to 3%.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: A Boon Totem grants nearby Survivors 3% Haste that briefly persists after leaving its radius.
duration: Haste lingers 2/3/4 seconds outside the Boon range.
mechanics.oncePerTrialOrOtherLimits: One active Boon Totem per Survivor; equipped Boons apply to that totem.

editorial.summary: Create a 24-metre Boon zone that grants Survivors 3% Haste, lingering briefly after they leave the area.
useCases: Place the Boon near a strong connected chase area so multiple loops benefit from 3% Haste.
Stack the effect with other Boons on one Totem to lower the setup cost.
Use the short linger to carry the movement bonus into a transition out of the Boon radius.
counters: The Killer can snuff the Totem.
Three percent Haste is powerful only if the chase actually remains inside useful geometry.
Bad Totem placement can put the effect far away from every important chase.
pros: Teamwide Haste rather than owner-only value.
Three percent is enough to change some loop timings.
9.5/8.7-era version is stronger than its old 2% form.
cons: Map and Totem geometry determine most of the value.
analysis: Boon: Dark Theory is useful only conditionally because 3% Haste is a real chase modifier, but the effect is trapped inside a twenty-four-metre circle. When that circle covers a strong building or several connected tiles, the Killer can feel the difference immediately.

The perk becomes more efficient in a multi-Boon loadout. Shadow Step, Circle of Healing, Steadfast, and Dark Theory can all share one Totem, so the blessing action buys several effects rather than paying a full setup tax for 3% movement alone.

The problem is geography. A Boon behind a dead-zone corner might be safe from snuffing and still accomplish nothing. A perfect central Boon may influence multiple chases but also be obvious enough for the Killer to remove.
Dark Theory therefore has a higher ceiling than many similarly ranked niche perks but a lower floor than general chase tools. It is a zone-control perk, and the zone has to matter.
editorial.verdict: A real team chase buff with a map-shaped reliability problem. Dark Theory can make a strong area stronger, but cannot guarantee the match happens inside its circle.
